Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Acme Insurance Holdings Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Acme Insurance Holdings' third quarter earnings call. Joining me on the call today are David Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Rachel Kim, Chief Financial Officer; Mark Gonzalez, Chief Underwriting Officer; and Robert Kline, Chief Investment Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to David Thompson.

David Thompson: Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Acme Insurance Holdings' performance for the third quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by robust premium growth across our core lines, meaningful improvements in loss ratios through better frequency control and tech-enabled severity management, prudent capital deployment into high-return opportunities like new cyber products and bolt-on acquisitions, declining customer acquisition costs from digital channel shifts, and ongoing expense ratio efficiencies via automation and mix optimization. Our focus on the EagleEye AI platform and digital transformation continues to yield positive outcomes, enhancing underwriting precision and customer retention.

Rachel, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Rachel Kim: Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. As David mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $520 million, or $2.85 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included premium expansion, underwriting discipline, and steady investment returns. Our combined ratio was 92.5%, reflecting effective underwriting and claims management. Investment income for the quarter was $350 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with deployable excess capital at $4.2 billion and a statutory RBC ratio of 562%.

Before diving deeper, let me turn to our forward-looking premium growth outlook. As always, these statements are subject to the risks and uncertainties outlined in our SEC filings, including market volatility, catastrophe events, and regulatory changes. We're pleased to reaffirm our strong trajectory entering Q4 and FY 2025. For the fourth quarter of 2024, we guide to net premium growth of 8% to 10% year-over-year, driven by disciplined rate actions, robust retention, and selective new business expansion. Looking further ahead, we now expect full-year 2025 net written premium growth of 10% to 12%, up from our prior guidance of 9% to 11%, reflecting favorable reinsurance renewals at January 1st and accelerating momentum in our high-margin segments.

Breaking this down by our core lines of business, where we've seen tailored strategies yielding differentiated results. In Property & Casualty, which represents 60% of our book, we anticipate Q4 growth of 9% to 11%, with FY 2025 at 11% to 13%. Commercial P&C continues to lead, with embedded rate changes of +6.2% in Q3—ahead of peers like Travelers and Chubb—fueled by hardening market conditions in middle-market casualty and excess & surplus lines. Our catastrophe-exposed property book grew 7% in Q3, supported by rate increases of 8-10% in high-risk zones like Florida and California, where we've optimized attachment points and layered in more parametric triggers to mitigate secondary uncertainty from events like Hurricane Helene analogs.

Personal lines, at 25% of P&C, are guiding to 6% to 8% growth in Q4 and 9% to 11% for 2025. Auto premiums benefited from a +4.5% rate filing approval across 35 states, complemented by our telematics program—now penetrating 45% of our policies—which has improved risk selection and delivered a 2-point loss ratio improvement. Homeowners growth is tempered at 5% due to coastal re-underwriting, but we're countering this with bundled offerings tied to our new climate-resilient add-ons, inspired by innovations from Lemonade and Hippo.

Shifting to Specialty and Life & Health, which comprise 30% of our portfolio, we project 12% to 14% growth for Q4 and 13% to 15% in 2025. Cyber insurance remains a standout, with gross written premiums up 25% YTD on the back of surging demand amid ransomware spikes—think Change Healthcare-scale events. We've expanded capacity through our Lloyd's syndicate partnership, pricing at mid-90s combined ratios, well ahead of industry averages. Group health and accident lines are growing 10%, leveraging direct-to-employer distribution and AI-driven underwriting that has cut new business cycle times by 40%.

Regionally, our diversification is paying dividends. In the U.S., our largest market at 55% of premiums, Q4 growth guides to 9% to 11%, with FY 2025 at 11% to 13%, propelled by the $1.2 billion acquisition of Midwest Regional Mutual closing in Q1 '25, adding scale in workers' comp and agribusiness. Europe, at 25% of the book, expects more measured 5% to 7% growth, navigating Solvency II recapitalization and softening D&O rates post-IPOs slowdown; however, our UK motor telematics JV with Aviva is ramping to 150,000 policies by year-end. Asia-Pacific and Latin America, 20% of premiums, are the growth engines at 15% to 18% for both periods—India life sales surging 22% on bancassurance tie-ups akin to HDFC Ergo, and Brazil casualty expanding via micro-insurance platforms targeting the unbanked.

Key drivers underpinning this guidance include our 95.2% renewal retention rate—up 80 basis points YOY—sustained by customer-centric pricing algorithms and a 15% reduction in expense ratio through RPA automation in claims processing. Reinsurance terms renewed favorably at 1/1/25, with ceded premiums flat despite $500 million cat tower expansion, thanks to lower pricing from Bermuda reinsurers amid abundant capacity.

Strategically, we're leaning into tech-enabled growth: our EagleEye AI platform, now live across 80% of underwriting, has boosted quote conversion by 12% while flagging 18% more adverse selection risks. We're also piloting embedded insurance with fintech partners like Stripe and Shopify, targeting $300 million in GWP by mid-2025 in pay-per-use auto and cyber products. These initiatives position us to outpace the industry composite, which we see growing at 7-9% per AM Best forecasts, especially as rates normalize post the 2022-2024 hardening cycle.

Of course, risks remain: potential cat aggregation from La Niña patterns could pressure Q4 if above our $400 million tolerance, economic softening might hit commercial volumes, and regulatory scrutiny on AI fairness in California and the EU could delay filings. That said, our attritional loss ratio of 58% and 92% combined ratio provide ample buffer. This premium growth guidance reflects our disciplined execution in a resilient insurance market, positioning us for mid-teens EPS growth in 2025.

Now, turning to our core underwriting performance, focusing on loss ratio trends and the key drivers—primarily claims frequency and severity. Our consolidated loss ratio, defined as incurred losses and loss adjustment expenses divided by earned premiums, is a critical measure of our P&C segment's profitability. We're pleased to report a Q3 loss ratio of 68.5%, a 360 basis point improvement from 72.1% in Q3 last year, and down 140 basis points sequentially from Q2. This brings our nine-month loss ratio to 70.2%, positioning us well toward our full-year guidance of 69-71%.

Our loss ratio benefited from disciplined pricing actions over the past 18 months, which have flowed through to earned premiums at a robust 8.2% year-over-year growth. However, we continue to navigate elevated severity pressures from inflation and supply chain disruptions, partially offset by frequency moderation.

Claims frequency—measured as claims per 100 exposure units—declined 4.2% year-over-year across our book, our strongest quarterly improvement in two years. In personal auto, frequency fell 5.8%, driven by our UnityDrive telematics program, now penetrating 42% of our policies, up from 28% a year ago. This uses real-time driving data from partners like Verizon Connect to incentivize safer behaviors via usage-based insurance discounts, reducing at-fault accidents by an estimated 12% among participants. Commercial auto saw a milder 2.1% drop, tempered by lingering driver shortages in trucking, but our enhanced underwriting with EagleView aerial imagery for fleet risk assessment has helped stabilize this line.

In homeowners, frequency was flat at 1.12 claims per 100 policies, reflecting normalized weather patterns post-2023's active hurricane season. Workers' comp frequency improved 3.5%, aided by our Return-to-Work programs and integration of predictive analytics from vendors like Verisk, which flag high-risk claims early.

Severity remains the headwind, up 6.1% year-over-year to an average of $14,200 per claim. This is in line with industry peers like Progressive and Travelers. Key drivers include inflationary pressures: auto repair costs rose 7.2% due to OEM parts shortages and labor rates, exacerbated by chip shortage ripple effects, with body shop rates up 9% in key markets like California and Florida. Medical and litigation costs in workers' comp and liability lines climbed 8.4%, fueled by rising opioid alternatives and social inflation—nuclear verdicts exceeding $10 million, which we attribute to 15% of our large losses this quarter. Natural catastrophes totaled $245 million pre-tax, or 4.2 points to the loss ratio, primarily from California wildfires and Midwest hailstorms—20% below our cat budget thanks to refined RMS modeling.

Regionally, U.S. (72% of earned premiums) loss ratio was 67.8%, our best in five quarters. Southeast frequency held steady despite rate adequacy gains, but severity up 7% from storm activity. We've repriced 85% of our Florida homeowners book post-legislation, targeting 12% rate hikes. Europe (18%) improved to 71.2% from 76.5%, driven by 6% frequency declines in UK motor, though severity spiked 9% in Germany due to flood remediation and EU regulatory caps—our Allianz Re tower capped net exposure at 2.5 points. Asia-Pacific (10%) at 69.1%, with Australia commercial lines at 65% thanks to cyber exclusions amid ransomware like the Optus breach; Japan severity rose 5% from yen weakness.

Our edge comes from tech: GenAI-powered claims triage via UnityClaims has reduced cycle times by 28% and LAE by 15 basis points through auto-adjudication of 35% of low-dollar claims under $5,000. Pricing sophistication with machine learning on 500+ rating factors has unlocked 2.5 points of improvement—e.g., EV-specific factors for auto, cutting severity by 4%. We're doubling down on diversification: non-cat lines now 82% of the book, up from 78%, and expanding parametric insurance with Swiss Re for index-triggered payouts. Reinsurance costs rose modestly to 2.8% of premiums, but our 1-in-250 year retention keeps us agile.

Looking forward, Q4 loss ratio in the 68-70% range, assuming normalized cats. Frequency tailwinds from telematics to 50% penetration, severity moderation on supply chain easing—we've stress-tested for 5% CPI insurance inflation. Combined ratio guidance holds at 92-94%, underscoring ROE expansion above 12%.

I'll now touch on our capital deployment strategy. We ended the quarter with $4.2 billion in deployable excess capital, supported by strong ratios. Our allocation framework prioritizes returns above our 10% cost of equity. We've delivered mid-teens ROE through the cycle.

First, shareholder returns: Board approved a 12% dividend increase to $0.65 quarterly, $2.60 annualized—17th year of growth. New $1.2 billion repurchase authorization, remaining capacity $1.8 billion. Repurchased 4.2 million shares YTD at $142 average, 11% total yield.

Organic investments: $850 million to digital transformation. ApexNext platform with gen AI and telematics data reduced auto loss ratio 1.8 points. Partnered with Google Cloud for climate modeling amid $110 billion global NATCAT losses YTD per Swiss Re. U.S.: $300 million embedded APIs with Amazon/Shopify for 15% premium lift. Europe: $200 million blockchain smart contracts for D&O, 3-point expense shave. APAC: $150 million microinsurance via mobile wallets.

New products: $450 million seeding. Cyber Sentinel Suite for SMBs, $250 million new premiums Q3. Climate Resilience Parametric with Swiss Re, $180 million APAC. Longevity+ Annuity, $1 billion VNB projected.

M&A: Two deals $950 million. CyberForge Underwriters $600 million, $400 million GWP, $50 million synergies. 40% stake IndoPac Re $350 million for India. Tracking 15 more, 15% IRR minimum.

FY2024 deployment $3.5 billion: 35% returns, 25% organic, 20% products, 20% M&A—targets 13-15% ROE. Resilient with $7.5 billion reinsurance.

Next, customer acquisition cost—or CAC—trends, fully loaded cost per new policyholder. Q3 CAC at $218 per policy, 18% YoY decline from $265, 5% sequential from $229. TTM $232, below peer $280 per Deloitte. LTV/CAC 4.8x, up from 3.9x.

Digital shift: 62% personal auto DTC, CAC $162, AI underwriting <30s quotes, 28% conversion. Commercial $412 CAC, down 12%, embedded with QuickBooks/Stripe, 15,000 SMBs at $350. Programmatic ad 3.2x MER.

Regions: U.S. $195, 21% down, telematics 45%. Europe $285, up 4% GDPR, UK 14% drop via aggregators. APAC $260, 16% down micro embeds, throttling for 4x ratio.

Doubling high-LTV: Bundling cross-sell 32%, halves household CAC. Agent commissions 22% from 28%. Q4 $225-230, FY $225, LTV/CAC 5.2x.

Finally, expense ratio trends. Improved to 28.5% Q3, down 70 bps YoY from 29.2%, 140 bps sequential. TTM 28.9%, lowest since 2018 demutualization. FY track 28.7%, 220 bps better than 2023.

Commissions 12.4% from 13.1%, direct 28% new business vs 22% YoY, 5-7% vs 15-18% agents. U.S. 11.8% telematics, Europe 14.2% brokers, APAC 13.5% bancassurance.

OpEx 16.1%, absolute +4.2% to $1.42B. Salaries +6% offset offshore savings $25M. Tech $180M: STP 72% claims, AWS 22% data cut, NLP 40% review time. Marketing CAC $145, down 8%.

Regions: NA 15.4%, Europe 16.8% GDPR, APAC 17.2% micro. Downtrend from 17.3% 2020.

Outlook: Q4 28-29%, 2025 27.5-28.5%. Levers: insurtech APIs, AI LAE 15% cut, cyber M&A.

Mark, over to you for underwriting update.

Mark Gonzalez: Thank you, Rachel. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial P&C line. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including expanded use of EagleEye AI and parametric triggers.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the expected premium growth breakdown by region and line for 2025?

Rachel Kim: Good morning, Sarah. As I detailed earlier, our U.S. market at 55% guides 11-13% for FY2025, boosted by the Midwest acquisition. Europe 5-7% measured growth, APAC/LatAm 15-18% as engines. P&C 11-13%, specialty/L&H 13-15%. This is underpinned by 95.2% retention and favorable reins terms.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of ongoing inflation on loss ratio severity and your mitigations?

Rachel Kim: Good morning, Mike. Severity up 6.1% to $14,200, driven by 7.2% auto repairs and 8.4% med/lit costs. Mitigations include UnityClaims GenAI for 28% faster cycles, telematics at 42% penetration cutting frequency 4.2%, and ML pricing for 2.5-point gains. Q4 68-70% expected.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong: What is the expected impact of regulatory changes like AI scrutiny on your underwriting strategy and expense trends?

Mark Gonzalez: Good morning, Lisa. Regulatory focus in CA/EU on AI fairness is noted, but our EagleEye platform's transparency and 500+ factors position us well. For expenses, GDPR/MiFID added minor pressure in Europe, but direct mix to 35% by 2026 and RPA keep us at 28.7% FY. No material delays anticipated.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera: Can you elaborate on capital deployment, particularly new products and M&A pipeline?

Rachel Kim: Certainly, Tom. New launches like Cyber Sentinel with $250M Q3 premiums, parametric $180M APAC, and Longevity+ for $1B VNB. M&A: CyberForge accretive Q1'25, IndoPac for India growth. Pipeline of 15, targeting 15% IRR, maintaining 95% payout.

Operator: Our next question from Alex Chen with Citi. Please go ahead.

Alex Chen: How are CAC trends influencing your growth strategy, especially in APAC?

Rachel Kim: Alex, CAC down 18% YoY to $218, LTV/CAC 4.8x. In APAC, $260 down 16% via embeds in ride-hailing, but throttling to protect ratios. Tilting to commercial for longer tenures, bundling cross-sell at 32%.

Operator: [No further questions at this time.]

David Thompson: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Acme Insurance Holdings. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
